BTS and Guns N' Roses Boost Jakarta's Desires as a Global Concert Magnet 
 INDUSTRI HIBURAN BTS and Guns N' Roses Boost Jakarta's Desires as a Global Concert Magnet
 The concert featuring K-pop group BTS and American rock band Guns N' Roses is expected to further enhance Jakarta's appeal as a global event hub.
 13 Nov 2026 16:13 WIB · Metropolitan 
 AP
 Kecil Sedang Besar Sangat Besar Share
 Copy Link
 By Fransiskus Wisnu Wardhana Dany 
 This article has been translated using AI. See original . 
 00:00 00:00 10 10 1.00x Jakarta is set to welcome global artists once again. Following Kanye West's concert, "Ye Live in Jakarta 2026," on October 24-25, 2026, K-pop group BTS and American rock band Guns N' Roses will thrill their fans in Indonesia.
 The arrival of international artists is believed to enhance Jakarta's appeal, particularly as a magnet for international-level events.
 Guns N' Roses (GNR) first held a concert at the Gelora Bung Karno Madya Stadium, Senayan, Central Jakarta, on November 21. This concert also introduced two new singles, namely 'Nothin' and 'Atlas'.
 BTS will follow up with their 'Arirang' World Tour in Jakarta, scheduled for December 26-27 and 29 at the Gelora Bung Karno Main Stadium. 'Arirang' (2026) is their new album, which was released in March of this year.
 Maria DM (52) can hardly contain her excitement to see RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V, and Jung Kook perform. Her enthusiasm is heightened as this marks her first time attending a BTS concert in person.
 "Attending this concert is a gift to myself," said Maria on Friday (13/11/2026). She held a ticket for the third day of the concert, which she purchased for Rp 4 million.
 The third day of the concert coincided with V's birthday. Maria idolizes him the most among the other BTS members.
 She didn't have any special preparations for the upcoming concert. She just chose an Arirang-themed outfit based on the suggestion of her K-pop-loving nephew.
 "Also, prepare a healthy body so you can stand in line and wait for the concert to start. I'm afraid you'll be exhausted," joked Maria.
 Maria also supports the government's efforts to increase the number of music concerts and other events. In addition to affordable ticket prices, public transportation makes it easier and more comfortable for people from various backgrounds to attend.
 Syifa Fauziah, 22, is eagerly looking forward to watching BTS perform. She will attend the third day of the concert, coinciding with V's birthday celebration.
 "I almost couldn't attend, but last October I received a bonus from my company, and I was finally able to save up for a ticket," Syifa said. For the upcoming concert, she is preparing an outfit that fits the theme and is considering buying some accessories at the concert venue.
 Syfa hopes for more entertainment events in the future in Indonesia, especially featuring international artists who have a large fan base.
 "Attending a concert is not just about watching your favorite artist, but also about the experience and memories you can take home. Especially for those who are seeing BTS live for the first time, it’s bound to be an unforgettable experience," said Syifa.
 Public enthusiasm
 The promoter has made 25,000 tickets available for fans to see GNR's frontmen, Axl Rose, Slash, and Duff McKagan. The grandstand tickets have sold out, leaving only festival group tickets available.
 Tovic Raharja, the President Director of Rajawali Indonesia and promoter of the GNR concert at Jakarta's City Hall on Friday (13/11/2026), stated that GNR previously performed in Jakarta in 2018. However, this time will be different as it will feature a special appearance by nine of Indonesia's guitar legends.
 Meanwhile, BTS's concert promoters are offering tickets for 60,000 attendees each day of the concert. Tickets are already sold out.
 Iradat Ikrar Hartaman, a representative of iMe Indonesia as the promoter, estimates that around 50,000 domestic spectators and 10,000 international attendees will attend the BTS concert each day. This will have a dual impact on both the economy and tourism.
 Jakarta Governor Pramono Anung noted that one by one, global artist concerts are establishing the city as a key epicenter for international events. This was evident during the concert of Kanye West, "Ye Live in Jakarta 2026," which generated an impact of nearly Rp 450 billion.
 The Jakarta Running Festival also took place during Kanye's concert. The event generated an economic impact of Rp 175 billion.
 "This shows that the global public now has confidence in Jakarta. Hopefully, this will further enhance international public trust in Indonesia," said Pramono.
 Double impact
 Tourism Minister Widiyanti Putri Wardhana highlighted a similar point, noting that concerts and other events have a dual impact, including the opportunity to strengthen Indonesia's position as an international concert destination and a hub for music-based tourism.
 Widiyanti referenced findings from market research firm Grand View Research, which estimates that the global music tourism market will reach a value of $103.7 billion by 2025 and is projected to grow to $330 billion by 2033. This potential is also evident in Indonesia, as seen with the impact of the concert "Ye Live in Jakarta 2026" featuring Kanye West.
 The positive momentum is expected to continue with the upcoming concerts of GNR and BTS. GNR aims to attract 22,000 attendees, including around 2,000 international tourists. Meanwhile, BTS is set to draw 180,000 fans, with more than 30,000 of them being foreign visitors.
 "The GNR and BTS concerts have the potential to generate tourist spending of up to Rp 158.3 billion, including accommodation, dining, transportation, and souvenirs," said Widiyanti.
 A number of strategies are being prepared to ensure that tourist destinations, shopping centers, and other venues are bustling before, during, and after the concert. The Ministry of Tourism is collaborating with InJourney to optimize Sarinah, Taman Mini Indonesia Indah (TMII), and the airports.
 Garuda Indonesia is preparing a special flight experience for Army, BTS fans traveling to Jakarta, featuring a special announcement, visual displays of BTS, and a purple ambiance set up from their arrival at the airport.
 "There is a special moment we want to highlight: Indonesia will host the final concert of BTS's Asia tour in 2026. Even more special, the last concert on December 29 will be broadcast live to cinemas in over 80 countries and regions through approximately 2,800 screens worldwide," said Widiyanti.
 This is part of Jakarta's promotion, not just as a concert venue but also as a tourist destination to a global audience.
 The Ministry of Tourism, through its flagship program "Event by Indonesia," has organized 160 events by September 2026, with an estimated economic impact of Rp 22.14 trillion.
 "We want fans to come for the music they love, enjoy a memorable experience, and leave with beautiful stories about Indonesia," Widiyanti said.
